title: Normalize compressed attachments to guarantee correct quota debits for interleaved multipart uploads
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We observed several customer-reported and internally-detected cases where token and byte debits were inconsistent for requests that: (a) upload prompts and attachments in multiple interleaved frames, (b) use client-side compression (gzip/deflate) for attachments, and (c) trigger on-the-fly model fallback or routing. Root causes found during initial triage:

- Tokenization sometimes occurs before server-side decompression, so compressed bytes are treated as opaque input and produce wildly different token counts than the eventual decoded content.
- The rate-limiter and quota subsystem currently reserves/charges an upfront provisional debit at request start. When attachments arrive late or are replayed, we either overcharge (double-reserve) or undercommit (rollback missed finalization).
- Multipart chunking logic can produce non-idempotent ledger events when the same upload-id is retried through different proxies; this causes duplicate debits if dedupe keys are not canonicalized to decompressed content hashes.

Scope: Fix metering correctness for interleaved multipart uploads with client-side compression and ensure predictable interaction with rate limiting and fallback routing. This ticket focuses on the server-side canonicalization path and metering service changes; separate follow-ups will handle client SDK guidance and proxy-level streaming optimizations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Server always computes token/byte debits from canonicalized, decompressed content for attachments before committing final ledger entries.
2) Provisional reserve semantics updated: initial reserve limited to prompt-only tokens; attachments reserve deferred until decompression and first successful tokenization. Edge cases (attachments timeout/never-arrive) must auto-revert provisional reserves within configurable TTL.
3) Upload idempotency: ledger writes use a canonical dedupe key derived from (upload_id, decompressed_sha256) to avoid duplicate charges across retries/proxies.
4) E2E tests added that simulate interleaved uploads, replayed frames, and compressed attachments yielding same final debit across retries.
5) No regression in streaming latency >2% p50 for normal prompt-only requests.
6) Live canary rollout behind feature-flag with monitoring dashboards and an alert for >0.1% unexpected debit variance for the canary cohort.
tasks: Add decompression normalization step in ingress pipeline before tokenization (server-side only)
Change provisional debit policy: reserve for prompt at start; defer attachment debit until tokenization commit or TTL expiry
Implement canonical dedupe key = sha256(decompressed_bytes) + upload_id for ledger idempotency
Extend metering service API to accept "canonicalized_size" and "canonicalized_hash" fields
Add unit tests for tokenization on decompressed payloads and for retry/dedup scenarios
Build e2e harness that replays interleaved gzipped frames via test proxy
Prepare rollout plan: feature flag, canary cohort, monitor, rollback plan
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after reproducing customer report (support-11023). Initial triage indicates decompression ordering bug in ingress proxy. Blocking: need decision whether to decompress at edge proxy or central metering service.

2026-03-11 - Ethan Zhao: Ran quick POC: decompressing at ingress eliminates tokenization mismatch but adds ~6-8ms p50 for requests with small attachments. Suggest decompress at edge but send canonicalized hash to metering service to avoid moving large bytes around.

2026-03-12 - Design review (María Gómez): Approved canonical-hash approach; two constraints: (1) proxies must compute decompressed sha256 streaming (no full buffering when possible), (2) fallback paths must be able to compute hash if proxy can't (metering service will compute as fallback).
2026-03-12 - Engineering note: Dependency ENG-555001 (kvcache warmup overcharge detector) must land first to ensure combined alerting in canary. Marking dependency accordingly.

2026-03-13 - PR opened by Ethan (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345): Adds decompression normalization and new ledger dedupe key. Requesting review from @lisa-nguyen and @omar-rahman for rate-limiter interactions.

2026-03-13 - Lisa Nguyen: Reviewed. Left two comments: (a) ensure streaming sha256 uses consistent chunk size across proxies to avoid different intermediate chunking, (b) provisional reserve TTL should be configurable per-customer (enterprise tenants may require longer windows).

2026-03-13 - QA: Added smoke tests for replayed frames; found a case where partial decompression failure led to lost rollbacks. QA recommends adding explicit rollback path and metric provisional_reserve_rollbacks.
